questions.question_text: Which term is a **like term** with $6m$?

options.why: Different variable — $n$ is not $m$, so a matching coefficient does not help.
Different power — $m^2$ is not $m$, even though both have coefficient $6$.
A constant has no variable part, so it is unlike a term in $m$.

questions.solution_text:
$6m$ has variable part $m$
$-2m$ also has variable part $m$
The coefficient does not matter
$-2m$

questions.question_text: Which term is a **like term** with $5j^2k$?

options.why: The powers are swapped; $jk^2$ has $k^2$, not $j^2$, so it is unlike.
Dropped the $k$; a missing variable makes the terms unlike.
Extra power on $k$; $k^1$ and $k^2$ differ, so the terms are unlike.

questions.solution_text:
$5j^2k$ has variable part $j^2k$
$4j^2k$ has variable part $j^2k$
Same variables, same powers
$4j^2k$

questions.question_text: Which term is a **like term** with $-7$?

options.why: Matched the number $7$; $-7d$ carries the variable $d$, so it is unlike a constant.
$27f$ carries the variable $f$; only plain numbers are like $-7$.
Read the coefficient $7$ as the whole term; $7x$ still has a variable.

questions.solution_text:
$-7$ is a plain number, with no variable part
$12$ is also a plain number
All constants are like terms
$12$

questions.question_text: Which terms in $7f + 7g - 3f + 3$ are like terms?

options.why: Matched the coefficient $7$ instead of the variable; $f$ and $g$ are different.
Included $7g$, which has variable $g$, not $f$.
Paired a variable term with the constant $3$; a constant is not like $-3f$.

questions.question_text: Which term is **unlike** the other two: $6ab$, $\frac{a}{b}$, $7ab$?

options.why: $6ab$ and $7ab$ share the variable part $ab$; the odd one divides by $b$.
Chose by the largest coefficient; $7ab$ still has variable part $ab$.

questions.solution_text:
$6ab$ has variable part $ab$
$7ab$ has variable part $ab$
$\frac{a}{b}$ divides by $b$ instead of multiplying by it
$\frac{a}{b}$

questions.question_text: In $14s - 3y - 3x + 14x$, which are the like terms?

options.why: Matched the coefficient $14$; $s$ and $x$ are different variables.
Matched the coefficient $-3$; $y$ and $x$ are different variables.
Included $-3y$, which has variable $y$, not $x$, so it does not belong.
